raw_case_text:
A 40-year-old male traveling from Bangladesh was admitted with fever and joint pain at Nakasero Hospital on 09 Sep 2017. Date of initial symptom onset of illness was 08 Sep 2017. The patient had no significant past medical history, was on no regular medication, and had received yellow fever specific travel-related vaccination. The patient, whose final destination was the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) where he worked, became ill while in transit in Dubai before traveling to Uganda. Once in Uganda and at Nakasero Hospital, a blood sample was collected on 09 Sep 2017 and transported to the arbovirus laboratory at UVRI.
Less detailed information is available for case report 2 involving two sisters who traveled to Ethiopia to visit their father for about 6 weeks. They became ill but got better after a week with treatment in Ethiopia. Their father had been diagnosed with a case of DF 2 months prior to them falling sick. They traveled back to Uganda on 27 Aug 2017. They arrived at the UVRI clinic on 03 Oct 2017, and a blood sample was collected from each person, approximately 5 weeks post-travel. They looked well but requested a DF test to confirm test results performed in Ethiopia.
A total of 284 serum samples collected in 2017 were tested for yellow virus (YFV), West Nile virus (WNV), DENV1-4, CHIKV and Zika virus (ZIKV) antibodies by IgM capture ELISA. Only the diagnostic testing results for arbovirus infections of the three travel-related cases are shown and summarized in Table 1. All serological testing in case report 1 (ARB01183/Uganda) were negative, while high neutralizing antibodies against DENV2 were found for both sisters that traveled to Ethiopia in case report 2 (ARB01227UVRI and ARB01228UVRI). 
Virus culture on Vero cell monolayers was performed in T25 flasks. The serum sample from the Bangladeshi traveler exhibited prominent and characteristic 100% CPE on day 2 post-infection. RNA extracted from harvested virus supernatant and tested by group-specific RT-PCR was positive for alphavirus and negative for flavivirus and bunyavirus. Further testing by real-time RT-PCR using CHIKV, ONNV and Semliki Forest virus (SFV) specific primers, yielded positive results for CHIKV. Next generation sequencing of the RNA isolated from cell culture supernatant of the CPE-positive culture sample identified a CHIKV genome that genetically clustered within a CHIKV clade containing predominantly Asian CHIKV strains (Fig. 1). The CHIKV strain most related to the virus isolated from ARB01183/Uganda was from Bangladesh collected in 2017 (MF77773566, Fig. 1 insert).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old male traveling from Bangladesh to the Democratic Republic of Congo presented in Uganda with a 1-day history of fever and joint pain, alongside two sisters returning to Uganda 5 weeks after an acute febrile illness in Ethiopia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Case 1 (40-year-old male) developed fever and arthralgia on September 8, 2017 while in transit in Dubai from Bangladesh to the DRC and was admitted to Nakasero Hospital in Uganda on September 9, 2017. Case 2 involved two sisters who developed a 1-week febrile illness while visiting their father in Ethiopia (who had been diagnosed with dengue fever 2 months earlier) and presented well to the UVRI clinic in Uganda on October 3, 2017 (5 weeks post-travel) for confirmatory testing.
subjective.past_medical_history: Case 1: no significant past medical history, no regular medications, vaccinated against yellow fever, traveled from Bangladesh via Dubai to Uganda/DRC. Case 2: two sisters with 6-week travel to Ethiopia where their father had dengue fever 2 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Case 1: fever and joint pain. Case 2 (two sisters): prior 1-week febrile illness in Ethiopia; asymptomatic at 5-week post-travel clinic visit.

objective.physical_examination: Case 1: febrile on admission. Case 2: both sisters appeared clinically well at 5 weeks post-travel.
objective.routine_investigations: Arbovirus IgM capture ELISA panel (YFV, WNV, DENV1-4, CHIKV, ZIKV) was negative in acute serum from Case 1 (ARB01183/Uganda), whereas Vero cell culture showed 100% cytopathic effect (CPE) on day 2 post-infection with positive alphavirus and CHIKV real-time RT-PCR (negative flavivirus and bunyavirus RT-PCR) and next-generation sequencing clustering with 2017 Bangladeshi Asian-clade CHIKV strains (MF77773566). In Case 2 (ARB01227UVRI and ARB01228UVRI), plaque reduction neutralization testing (PRNT) demonstrated high-titer neutralizing antibodies against dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) in both sisters.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Case 1: Imported acute chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection from Bangladesh, confirmed by Vero cell viral isolation, CHIKV real-time RT-PCR, and whole-genome NGS (with negative DENV1-4 IgM and flavivirus RT-PCR). Case 2: Confirmed convalescent dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) infections in two sisters returning from Ethiopia, established by high-titer DENV-2 neutralizing antibodies on PRNT.
